hippocratic-bedside-diagnosis.research_focus: classical Greek physicians, the Hippocratic school on Kos, ancient Greek clothing and bedside medicine as shown on vases and reliefs
hippocratic-bedside-diagnosis.scene: A bearded Greek physician in a draped himation kneels by a patient on a low couch, two fingers on the patient's wrist, studying the patient's face

herophilus-pulse-timing.research_focus: Hellenistic Alexandria, ancient water clocks (clepsydra), and Greek physicians of the 3rd century BCE
herophilus-pulse-timing.scene: A Greek physician holds a seated patient's wrist while watching water drip from a bronze bowl clepsydra on a stand beside them

wang-shuhe-pulse-classic.research_focus: Jin dynasty China, traditional Chinese pulse diagnosis at three wrist positions, period scholar's robes and bamboo or silk manuscripts
wang-shuhe-pulse-classic.scene: A Chinese physician in flowing Jin-era robes presses three fingertips along a patient's wrist, a bundle of bamboo slips unrolled on the table beside them

leeuwenhoek-blood-cells.research_focus: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek's tiny single-lens brass microscopes in 1670s Delft and how red blood cells look under magnification
leeuwenhoek-blood-cells.scene: A Dutch merchant holds a tiny flat brass microscope up to a window, its pin bearing a drop of blood; inset beside him, a circle of rounded blood cells floating

auenbrugger-chest-percussion.research_focus: 18th-century Vienna medicine, Leopold Auenbrugger's percussion of the chest, period wigs and frock coats

bozzini-light-conductor.research_focus: Philipp Bozzini's 1806 Lichtleiter, a vase-shaped metal lantern with a candle, mirror and attached speculum tubes

berger-eeg-recorded.research_focus: Hans Berger in 1920s Jena, early galvanometer recording equipment, electrodes on the scalp and wavy traces on paper or film

papanicolaou-smear-test.research_focus: George Papanicolaou's 1920s New York laboratory, glass microscope slides and stained cells

forssmann-heart-catheter.research_focus: Werner Forssmann's 1929 self-catheterisation at Eberswalde, a thin urinary catheter through the arm vein, and the X-ray that confirmed it

apgar-score-newborns.research_focus: 1950s American hospital delivery rooms, newborn assessment, nurses' and anaesthesiologists' uniforms of the era

hirschowitz-fibre-optic-endoscope.research_focus: the first fibre-optic gastroscope of 1957, its flexible bundle of glass fibres and eyepiece

first-ct-scan-patient.research_focus: the 1971 EMI head scanner at Atkinson Morley Hospital, London, and the first grainy cross-sectional brain images

home-pregnancy-test-launched.research_focus: 1970s home pregnancy test kits with a small test tube, dropper and mirrored base, and 1970s bathroom interiors

first-hiv-blood-test.research_focus: 1985 blood bank laboratories, ELISA plates with rows of small wells, donated blood bags

fmri-brain-imaging.research_focus: early 1990s MRI scanners used for functional brain imaging, and fMRI brain maps showing active regions
fmri-brain-imaging.scene: A brain seen in cross-section with a few small regions glowing brightly, the round opening of a scanner behind it

capsule-endoscopy-camera-pill.research_focus: the 2000 wireless capsule endoscope, a pill-sized clear capsule holding a tiny camera, lens, lights and battery
capsule-endoscopy-camera-pill.scene: A clear pill-sized capsule with a tiny camera lens and lights at one end, resting on a fingertip, its innards visible through the shell
